answer: Behavioral plume clustering. Each agent action emits a feature trail (timing, call graph shape, resource use); a detector fits mixtures to these trails and flags tight sub-populations whose internal correlation exceeds a baseline. To survive, an attacker must decorrelate every puppet, adding independent delays and varied call paths. That cost is real per-identity work; when correlation exceeds the meadow baseline, the whole shared hollow of accounts gets frozen pending review.
